independent_semantic_review.scope: Independent semantic and hygiene review of the supplement-30 R1 source and guide, against answers 26/30 and owner decision 17. Approval is for provisional typed freeze only; publication metadata and final checks are separate.
review_details: KernelRef.hidden carries only a Fin n slot. hiddenKernel and resolveKernel select existing Seed constructors using the installation role; the three exact branch equations preserve known kernels and identify both hidden branches. Slot allocation and enforcing the role at each installation remain documented interpreter obligations.

The guide cites the existing totality of both seed constructors, gives exact 1/0 and 0/1 counter orientation, and does not infer seed-independent installation acceptance from the type alone: vacancy, phase, role-use checks, shared lazy draw and installation behavior must still be implemented and proved.

FirstMaterial, all candidate/ticket/commit/discard operations and proofs, privateSend, and their effect/cost categories are absent from the source. Caps.derivations is precisely Budget.sends + 51 * Budget.receives; no transient or private-send term remains.

Frame uses one allowance per existing Fin 14 query class and effect category, uniformly for all query payloads and handler states. Caps.envTotal sums Budget.cap times this finite allowance. Startup coins are separately bounded; no composition or global budget theorem is asserted.

The six environment commands are exactly create/bundle/accept/build/finish/hmac. The four record commands, all native uniform calls, and public BLAKE2b bypass the environment. Environment effects expose no record action, private ledger read, seed or kernel read, or shared cache read.

program preserves the existing CE secrecy wrapper and asModeO, now with explicit serverKid forwarded unchanged. Adversary and ledger coins share coinLift; test/fresh sends route through native record branches. Actual mode-O plaintext stays available to the private ledger before public mode-P projection.

Environment.start remains the agreed optional full-Created startup program. The same constructor result is handed to the private world and encoded for the eventual output. The guide explicitly leaves the actual CE constructor distribution/source equality to CE; retaining full Created and InactivePhase is allowed by supplement 30.

The guide accurately preserves the production failed-finish ordering: full raw receive precedes the sequence-one gate. C7 is an outstanding CE-owned exact observed/later-behavior erasure equality, not a new premise, axiom, proved fact, or claim that discarded kernel state erases hash effects.

The future result requirements include exact produced : List (FrameTag × PqxdhDeploymentNative.Frame), original serverTag/beaconTag/produce logging, failed-writer production retention, no registration frame logging, and raw-attempt counters. It explicitly says the existing program result is insufficient and no game projection is yet defined.

C2 is split into C2a finite resource Frame for env_g, C2b interpreter enforcement, and C2c correct hidden-entry designation. C7 is separate; C1 and C5 remain CE applications rather than record-lift hypotheses. Post/reveal support is deferred until R6 and LQ-F.

The five theorems are only exact kernel-resolution branches and source reply-type equalities. They add no cryptographic, independence, freshness, decoder or source-provenance assumption. The source does not refer to any H7 forbidden constant; transitive imports are not confused with direct forbidden-name use.

Guide limitations accurately state that the private interpreter, installation invariants, source simulation, chain/CTX hybrids, event bounds and ideal-world security facts are unfinished. No current probabilistic RecordLift.game or security theorem is claimed.
